subject: Handling R CMD check "no visible binding for global variable" errors

messages.author: a79eb65f0eae8655
messages.subject: Handling R CMD check "no visible binding for global variable" errors
parts:
So, I have a bunch of ggplot2-based functions that are (and always have been) throwing R CMD check warnings. Here's an example of such a function

  JitteredResponsesByContrast <- function (data) {
    return(
      geom_point(
               aes(
                 x = x.values, 
                 y = y.values
               ),
               data     = data,
               position = position_jitter(height = 0, width = GetDegreeOfJitter(jj))
      )
    )
  }

And the corresponding R CMD check warning:

granovagg.contr : JitteredResponsesByContrast: no visible binding for
  global variable ‘x.values’
granovagg.contr : JitteredResponsesByContrast: no visible binding for
  global variable ‘y.values’

The problem (which I think I understand now) is that x.values and y.values are variables defined in the data frame that gets handed in. That's *why* I'm using the data = argument to geom_point(). But, since R CMD check sees no obvious binding (they're not defined globally or even within the JitteredResponsesByContrast function), it panics.

Here are my questions: 
  1. do other people get these warnings?
  2. Are the warnings fair, since I'm playing well within the rules of ggplot2 syntax?
  3. How have people addressed this to get their packages to pass R CMD check without errors and warnings?
ggplot2 v0.8.9, for example, is on CRAN even though it has exactly these kinds of warnings: http://www.R-project.org/nosvn/R.check/r-patched-linux-ix86/ggplot2-00check.html

messages.subject: Re: Handling R CMD check "no visible binding for global variable" errors
parts:
They are just notes, aren't they? You dont need to worry about them - it's a fundamental limitation of the way the code checking works. 

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Handling R CMD check "no visible binding for global variable" errors
parts:
Hadley,

Thanks for your support. You're absolutely right.

When I submitted my package, Brian Ripley sent me a terse (and in hindsight, ambiguous) email response saying I needed to fix things before my package could be accepted. I thought he was saying my package was rejected because of the global variable binding messages, so I assumed they were warnings.

It now seems they're clearly notes, and therefore not (in an of themselves) grounds for excluding my package from CRAN.

I'm sorry to everyone for the confusion, and thanks again for helping me understand the difference between notes and warnings.

- Brian
